title: EV Charging Support Voice Agent
summary: A voice agent for EV drivers at a charger: reads live charger status and faults, guides fixes or approved remote actions, raises refunds and escalates safety issues to people.

seo.title: EV Charging Support Voice Agent | VipraTech
seo.description: Voice agent for charge point operators and EV fleets: charger status, guided fixes, approved remote actions, refunds and safety escalation.

designed_for: Head of Operations at a Charge Point Operator

problem.intro: EV drivers call for help while standing at a charger, often at night or on a highway, with a session that will not start, a payment that went through without charging or a connector that will not release. Support agents switch between the charge point management system, payment records and the app to work out what happened.

pain_points.title: Drivers need help in the moment
pain_points.detail: A driver at a dead charger cannot wait in a queue, and every minute affects the rest of the trip.

pain_points.title: Too many tools per call
pain_points.detail: Agents look up charger status, session logs, fault codes and payments in separate systems before they can help.

pain_points.title: Payment-without-charging disputes
pain_points.detail: Deducted payments with failed or short sessions turn into refund requests that need evidence from logs.

pain_points.title: Safety calls mixed with routine issues
pain_points.detail: Reports of a burning smell, a damaged cable or water near a charger must reach people at once.

solution.overview: We build a voice agent for your support line that identifies the station and connector from the caller's description, the station name or the ID printed on the charger. It reads live status, connector state, recent fault codes and session logs from your charge point management system. It walks the driver through troubleshooting steps written for that charger model and connector type and, where your operations team allows, triggers remote actions such as starting, stopping or resetting a session, each one logged. It checks payment and session records and raises refunds within policy. Any mention of smoke, burning, damaged cables or water sends the call to a person and alerts field operations.
capabilities: Identifies station and connector from station name, charger ID or location
Reads live charger status, connector state, fault codes and session logs from the CPMS
Guided troubleshooting by charger model and connector type
Triggers remote start, stop or reset only from an allow-list your operations team approves
Checks payment and session records and raises refund requests within policy
Immediate human escalation for smoke, burning smell, damaged cables or water

workflow.title: Identify the charger
workflow.detail: The agent identifies the station and connector, and confirms the vehicle is plugged in where relevant.

workflow.title: Screen for safety
workflow.detail: Any description of smoke, burning, sparks, damaged cables or water sends the call to a person and alerts field operations.

workflow.title: Read charger state
workflow.detail: Live status, faults and the latest session log are read from the CPMS.

workflow.title: Guide or act
workflow.detail: The agent guides the driver through model-specific steps or triggers an approved remote action.

workflow.title: Check the outcome
workflow.detail: If charging still does not start, the call is handed to a support agent with the diagnostics, and a field ticket is raised.

workflow.title: Close and refund
workflow.detail: Outcomes are logged, and refunds for failed sessions are raised within policy limits.

inputs: Charger status, fault codes and session logs from the CPMS
Troubleshooting guides for each charger model
Station directory with charger IDs and locations
outputs: Resolved sessions and logged remote actions
Fault trends by station and charger model
human_in_the_loop: Safety reports, repeated faults and refunds above policy limits go to people. Remote actions are limited to an allow-list approved by your operations team, and support leads review command logs.
integrations: Charge point management system using OCPP
Helpdesk such as Freshdesk or Zendesk
guardrails: Remote commands limited to an approved allow-list, with no configuration or firmware changes
Safety keywords trigger immediate human transfer
Drivers are never asked to handle damaged equipment
Session and payment verification before any refund
Every remote command logged with caller, charger and outcome
compliance_notes: Driver phone numbers, vehicle details and charging locations are personal data handled under the DPDP Act 2023.
Electrical safety and installation compliance of chargers remain the operator's responsibility; the agent supports drivers and logs actions.

pilot.scope: One region or highway corridor of your network, covering the most common issue types such as session start failures and payment without charging.
deliverables: Troubleshooting playbooks for the pilot charger models
Agent connected to CPMS and payments in test
Live pilot with call and command logs

what_we_measure.how: Share of pilot calls where charging started or the issue was closed by the agent, checked against session logs.
Time from call start to a successful session for resolved calls.
Refund decisions reviewed against session and payment evidence.
Scripted test calls plus review of live calls mentioning hazards.

faqs.q: Can the agent control our chargers?
faqs.a: Only through the remote actions your operations team puts on the allow-list, such as remote start, stop or reset, and only after confirming the station and connector. Configuration changes and firmware updates are never available to the agent.

faqs.q: Which charge point management systems do you support?
faqs.a: Any CPMS that exposes status, session and command APIs, typically built on OCPP. We confirm the available endpoints with your platform team before the pilot.

faqs.q: Can it support drivers round the clock?
faqs.a: Yes. The agent answers at any hour, and safety calls and complex cases are routed to your on-call staff according to your escalation rota.
Hindi, English and Hinglish, plus regional languages along your network's routes. Highway corridors often cross language boundaries, so the agent detects language at the start of each call.
